name: Threadmark
shortDescription: A planned companion for Apple Mail: private notes, tags and follow-ups kept beside the conversation.
longDescription: An email thread usually carries context that does not belong in the email itself — what you are waiting for, what was agreed on the phone, which project it relates to. Threadmark is being planned as a way to keep that context next to the conversation instead of in your head. The intent is a lightweight companion to Apple Mail rather than a replacement for it, and deliberately not a CRM. Nothing here is built yet, and the shape of the product may still change.
statusNote: In planning. This describes the intended direction, not finished software.
highlights: Planned: private notes attached to Apple Mail conversations
Planned: tags, follow-up dates and project context
Intended to leave the original message untouched
Intended to work without an account

features.title: Context where the conversation is
features.description: The core idea: attach a note, a tag or a follow-up date to a thread and find it again from the thread itself, rather than in a separate app you have to remember to open.

features.title: A companion, not a replacement
features.description: Threadmark is intended to sit alongside Apple Mail and leave your existing mail workflow as it is. How closely it can integrate depends on what Apple's mail extension APIs allow, which is still being assessed.

features.title: Annotations meant to stay yours
features.description: The design goal is that notes are private, stored on your Mac, and never sent to anyone in the conversation.

privacyNote: The intended design keeps notes and metadata on your Mac, with no Threadmark account and no upload of email content. This is a design goal for a product that does not exist yet, not a description of shipped behaviour.
